pr_body:
If an index request contains a type that is different to the type defined on the
index, we fail the request with an error.  However, this check happens fairly
late on in the process, and if the index request has generated dynamic updates
that conflict with the existing mappings on the index then merge errors will
get thrown instead.  This is confusing to users, as it is not at all obvious why
these conflicting mappings have been generated.

This commit adds a check for valid types early in the indexing process, so that
requests with invalid types will be failed with a more informative error message.

Fixes #77411
pr_title: Fail early if an index request has the wrong type
pr_comment: Note that this applies only to 7x - in 8x types are either not present on the request at all or are stripped out by the rest compatibility layer.
Changes look good to me. Can we also have this validation for delete operations? Thanks @romseygeek.

review_comment: Another naive question (sorry): could we catch this in `MapperService#merge` rather than relying on callers checking they're not adding a type first? Not to say there's anything wrong with checking it here, just that there's a risk there's more code paths that aren't covered. Maybe not today but possibly in a future version.

Types are gone entirely in 8x so I'm not that concerned about future new code paths.  I did initially try detecting this in `MapperService#merge` but that ended up breaking loads of unit tests which aren't being careful with their types, so I felt that this was the best fix for the minimum footprint.
Ok, makes sense, I also expect this won't change too much in what's left of the 7.x series. I would like this to be reviewed by someone who knows more about mappings than me, but this LGTM.
